# AudienceIntent

> AudienceIntent gets businesses recommended by AI. It is an Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) company in Wellington, Florida, USA, with one fully managed service: AI Recommended™. When people ask ChatGPT, Google AI or Perplexity who to hire or what to buy, AudienceIntent works to get the client's business named in the answer.

Last updated: 2026-11-13

Key facts:

- Tagline: "We get your business recommended by AI."
- Founded in 2024 by Kevin Bovett (founder and CEO). Based in Wellington, Florida. Works with businesses across the United States.
- One service only: AI Recommended™, a done-for-you monthly AEO service. AudienceIntent is not a software tool. A real team does the work.
- Price: $1,997/month for the first 90 days, then $997/month, month to month. Or $5,000 upfront for the first 90 days (saves $991).
- AI platforms tracked: ChatGPT, Google AI (AI Overviews and AI Mode) and Perplexity.
- Who it's for: local and small-to-mid-sized US businesses, from law firms, home services and insurance to gyms, wellness, tour operators and precious metals dealers.

## AI Recommended™: what's included every month

1. Open to crawlers: making sure ChatGPT, Google and Perplexity can reach and understand the website (robots.txt, llms.txt, sitemaps).
2. Website fixes: schema markup, sitemap and on-page fixes.
3. Customer question research: the real questions customers ask AI before they buy.
4. 4 new articles every month, built around those questions (Google leans heavily on recent content).
5. 4 older pages brought up to date every month.
6. Weekly visibility report: 50 prompts tracked every day.
7. Competitor tracking: up to 5 competitors.
8. A real human to talk to: a monthly progress call and a shared Slack channel.

How it runs: the first 90 days are the deep work (technical fixes, research, building the prompt library). From month 4 the focus is new content, refreshing older pages and tracking against competitors, and the price drops to $997/month on its own.

## Pricing

- Pay monthly: $1,997/month for a 90-day minimum, then $997/month, month to month.
- Pay upfront: $5,000 for the first 90 days (saves $991), then $997/month, month to month.
- Same price for every business, whatever its size.
- Nobody can guarantee a business will appear in a specific AI answer. AudienceIntent promises the work, done properly every month, and an honest report.

## Client results

- Vault Metal: AI mentions grew from 169 to 7,808 (+4,520%) and citations from 3 to 751 in 90 days.
- GoldenCrest Metals: visibility score up 202.4% in 90 days.
- Craft Food Tours: traffic from AI up 312% in 90 days.

## Common questions

- What is AEO? Answer Engine Optimization means making sure tools like ChatGPT, Google AI and Perplexity can find a business, understand what it does, and recommend it when someone asks for help.
- Is AEO different from SEO? They work together. SEO helps a business rank in a list of links. AEO helps it get named in the answer. AI tools still lean on search results, but they also weigh reviews, what other websites say about the business, and whether its content answers real questions clearly.
- How do AI tools decide who to recommend? They pull from the website, Google Business Profile, reviews, directories, articles and forums. They favour businesses that are clear about what they do, consistent everywhere, and mentioned by sources they trust.
- How long until results show? Perplexity can pick up a new page within a couple of weeks. Google AI and ChatGPT usually take two to three months to recommend a business on a steady basis. That is why the service starts with 90 days.
- Is a new website needed? No. AudienceIntent works with the existing site: WordPress, Wix, Squarespace, Shopify or custom.
- What does the client need to provide? Access to the website and Google Business Profile (or an intro to whoever runs them), plus a monthly progress call.

## AEO video answers

- [Video 01: What Is AEO? Answer Engine Optimization Explained](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/what-is-aeo/): AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) is the work of helping AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity find, understand and recommend your business. When someone asks AI who to hire or where to go, it can return a short list of recommendations. AEO helps your business become one of those names.
- [Video 02: Does Anyone Actually Use AI Search?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/does-anyone-use-ai-search/): Yes, people use AI search to decide who to hire and what to buy, including local business recommendations. The video describes adoption across several AI tools and shows how specific customer questions can signal that someone is close to a decision.
- [Video 03: AEO vs SEO: What's the Difference?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/aeo-vs-seo/): SEO aims to get your pages ranked in search results, while AEO aims to get your business named in an AI answer. A strong Google ranking does not guarantee a ChatGPT mention, so the video recommends keeping SEO and adding work on AI visibility.
- [Video 04: Which AI Engines Actually Matter?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/which-ai-engines-matter/): The video recommends starting with ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google's AI Overviews. Check each separately because their answers and source preferences differ, and a good result in one can hide an absence in another.
- [Video 05: What Is a Prompt, and Why Is It the New Keyword?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/what-is-a-prompt/): A prompt is the full question someone asks AI, expressed in natural language. Unlike a short keyword, it can include the problem, location, urgency and decision someone needs help with, which can change the businesses named in the answer.
- [Video 06: Branded vs Unbranded Prompts: Where AEO Is Won and Lost](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/branded-vs-unbranded-prompts/): A branded prompt includes your business name, while an unbranded prompt asks about a service or need without naming you. Check both: branded questions show how AI describes you, and unbranded questions show whether it introduces you to someone who has not chosen a business yet.
- [Video 07: Where Do You Find the Questions Your Customers Ask?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/where-to-find-customer-questions/): Find customer questions in sales calls, support emails, Reddit and online forums rather than guessing. Combine them into one list, then prioritise the questions a new customer would ask before choosing a business like yours.
- [Video 08: How Does AI Decide Who to Recommend?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/how-ai-decides-who-to-recommend/): The video highlights three things that help AI understand and assess a business: clear information, consistent details across the web and independent support from other people. These give engines more information to work with, but do not guarantee a recommendation.
- [Video 09: Where Does Each AI Engine Get Its Information?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/where-ai-engines-get-information/): The video describes AI answers as drawing on training information and live web lookups, with different engines leaning on different sources. It presents those source preferences as tendencies that can change, not fixed rules that guarantee a mention or citation.
- [Video 10: Is My Business Showing Up in AI Right Now?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/is-my-business-showing-up-in-ai/): Check ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google with three types of question: an unbranded recommendation, a comparison with a competitor and a question naming your business. Record whether you appear, whether the details are accurate and which other businesses are named, then treat the results as a snapshot rather than a stable ranking.
- [Video 11: Why Is AI Recommending My Competitor Instead of Me?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/why-ai-recommends-my-competitor/): AI recommending a competitor does not establish that their service is better. The video identifies four information gaps to investigate: an unclear website, few recent reviews, inconsistent business details and limited independent mentions.
- [Video 12: What If AI Is Saying the Wrong Thing About My Business?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/what-if-ai-says-the-wrong-thing/): Trace the incorrect answer to its sources, correct outdated listings or pages and publish accurate hours, services and location on your own website. Check the tone of the description as well as the facts, and allow for variable update times rather than expecting an immediate correction in every engine.
- [Video 13: How Does AEO Work, and Can I Do It Myself?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/how-aeo-works-can-i-do-it-myself/): AEO is a repeating process of finding customer questions, making your website readable, publishing answers, building evidence on other sites and tracking results. You can do it yourself, but the video stresses the ongoing time required for tools, technical work, content and keeping up with changes.
- [Video 14: Is AEO Right for My Business?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/is-aeo-right-for-my-business/): AEO is worth considering when customers research before buying, a new customer has meaningful value and your business already has a website and some reviews. It is not a quick fix for leads this week, and the video recommends building the basics first if you are starting without a website or reputation.
- [Video 15: How Long Does AEO Take to See Results?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/how-long-does-aeo-take/): The video suggests using about 90 days as an initial review period, not a guaranteed results deadline. Early movement may come sooner, but progress depends on your starting point, competition and how quickly different engines pick up changes.
- [Video 16: How Do You Track AEO?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/how-do-you-track-aeo/): Track the same customer questions word for word each day across the AI engines and locations you serve. Assess trends over weeks and keep each engine's results separate so a strong combined average does not hide an engine where you are absent.
- [Video 17: How Do I Know AEO Is Working?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/how-do-i-know-aeo-is-working/): Watch four measures: how often AI names your business, your share of brand mentions, your average position when named and the tone of the description. Review each engine separately as well as any overall average; the example in the video illustrates these measures rather than promising the same results.
- [Video 18: AEO Recap: What Should You Do Next?](https://www.audienceintent.ai/videos/aeo-recap-what-to-do-next/): Start by asking AI questions about your business and checking whether it names you and describes you accurately. The series frames AEO as improving your chances of being included in relevant recommendations, supported by clear information, independent evidence and tracking across engines.
